# dropoff.lol

> Private, browser-to-browser (peer-to-peer) file sharing. No accounts, no registration, and no permanent uploads — files stream directly from one device to another over WebRTC using a one-time `dropoff.lol/receive/<id>` link.

Full details about the service, how it works, and its limits.

## Overview

dropoff.lol is a free, browser-based file sharing service. A sender picks files on their device, and the site generates a one-time `dropoff.lol/receive/<id>` link. Anyone who opens that link downloads the files directly from the sender's browser — the transfer happens peer to peer and never touches a dropoff.lol server.

It is built on WebRTC and is a progressive web-style single-page application. It requires a modern browser on desktop or mobile and works on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android.

## Why it exists

Most file sharing services upload your files to a cloud server first. That means files sit on someone else's infrastructure, may be scanned or retained, and can be tied to accounts. dropoff.lol takes a different approach: nothing is uploaded and nothing is stored, because the transferring browsers ARE the servers. Shared files go from one device directly to another.

## How it works

1. A sender opens https://dropoff.lol and picks one or more files.
2. The site connects the sender to a signaling server to bootstrap a peer-to-peer WebRTC connection and generates a link formatted `dropoff.lol/receive/<id>`.
3. The sender shares that link with the receiver any way they like.
4. The receiver opens the link, and the file(s) stream directly from the sender's browser to the receiver's browser.
5. Once the transfer completes, the link is no longer needed; nothing was uploaded or stored by dropoff.lol.

## Limits and requirements

- File size is constrained by the browser, not by dropoff.lol (there is no upload, so there is no server cap). Practical limits are roughly 1–2 GB on desktop Chrome, about 1 GB on Firefox, and a few hundred MB on iPhone/iOS Safari.
- The sender's tab must stay open for the duration of the transfer because the sender's browser is the source of the files.
- Both sides need an internet connection; the transfer is end-to-end between the browsers.
- There are no accounts, no file retention, and no cloud storage.
